extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, NIH peer reviewers (SRG members), Scientific Review Administrators, and NIH staff involved in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policies governing the initial and council-level peer review of NIH grant and training applications, including reviewer responsibilities, conflict-of-interest rules, human-subjects considerations, scoring procedures, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of initial peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the initial peer review is to evaluate and rate the scientific and technical merit of the proposed research or research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial review is performed by Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) managed by Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs) located in NIH Institutes and Centers. This criterion is the primary goal driving SRG evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-step peer review process (SRG then Advisory Councils)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of applications submitted to the NIH takes place in multiple steps: the initial step in Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) and a second level of peer review carried out by the NIH National Advisory Councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRGs perform the scientific/technical merit evaluation; National Advisory Councils provide additional review/advice and ensure cross-section representation of the US population for funding deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rosters of Scientific Review Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Rosters of the membership of NIH Scientific Review Groups are available for standing review committees as well as Special Emphasis Panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of rosters supports transparency about who is reviewing applications and can inform recusal/conflict-of-interest assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of the Peer Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: A general, high-level overview describing how peer review is conducted across NIH components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the foundational description of stages, roles, and procedures; consult for orientation before reading specific procedural documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary of Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of terms used in NIH peer review and related guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to ensure consistent interpretation of review terminology (e.g., 'impact', 'priority score').

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Procedures for Scientific Review Group Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures that govern how SRG meetings are conducted for the purpose of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes operational rules for SRG deliberations, voting, and handling of conflicts; reviewers should follow these procedures during meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: General guidance provided to reviewers about expectations, responsibilities, and how to conduct reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers reviewer conduct, confidentiality, scoring expectations, and use of review forms; forms and certification requirements may accompany these guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Review of Specific Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized guidance for reviewing particular application types or topic areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reviewers to consider application-specific issues (e.g., clinical research, training awards) and may modify standard review emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of New Investigator R01's
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how reviewers should evaluate R01 applications from new investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include expectations about evaluating investigator track record in context, potential, and need for additional emphasis on feasibility and mentoring plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR Scoring Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The scoring procedure used by the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) for evaluating applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes numeric scoring, use of criterion scores versus overall impact/priority score, and any CSR-specific scoring conventions (see CSR documentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A review approach intended to make review more efficient, eliminating unnecessary redundancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May change the process for discussion or scoring in certain cases; consult CSR/IC guidance for when streamlined review applies and how it affects scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Research Involving Natural Products Usually Prepared as Complex Mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Special review guidance for research involving natural products that are complex mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reviewers on how to assess studies with inherently complex materials, including characterization and reproducibility concerns specific to such research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Grant Application and Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and procedures governing modular budget applications and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects how costs are presented and evaluated; reviewers should be aware of modular budget constraints and how budget assessment is handled under this format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children as Participants in Research Involving Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance requiring consideration of whether children are included as research participants and how that inclusion is justified and protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must assess inclusion plans and protections for children per NIH policy and related human-subjects guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for New Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials and guidance targeted to new investigators preparing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps new applicants meet expectations; reviewers should consider these resources when evaluating experience and training aspects of applications from new investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Opportunities and Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on available funding mechanisms and the required application forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers use correct application types/mechanisms as context for expectations; applicants must use required forms for eligibility and proper review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and Assignment Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for submitting applications and how applications are assigned to SRGs and Institutes/Centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment determines which reviewers and council will evaluate the application; appropriate referral impacts fairness and subject-matter expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Grant Review Process Video
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia resource describing the NIH grant review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful training material for reviewers and applicants to understand review flow, roles, and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice to Investigators Submitting Clinical Research Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific advice for applicants proposing clinical research about common review considerations and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely addresses study design, human-subjects protections, inclusion criteria, data/safety monitoring, and other clinical-specific review points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of Initial Scientific Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and policies governing how applicants may appeal the outcomes of initial scientific peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes grounds for appeal, timelines, and what aspects of review can be challenged; applicants should follow prescribed appeal procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Announces Updated Criteria for Evaluating Research Grant Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated set of criteria (see NOT-OD-05-002) for evaluating research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes comparison documents and Q&A; represents formal changes to reviewer criteria—reviewers must apply the updated criteria when indicated by IC/CSR guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of Updated and Previous Criteria for Evaluating Research Grant Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Document comparing new NIH review criteria to prior criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps reviewers and applicants understand changes in emphasis or scoring; consult when transitioning between old and new criteria frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and Answers about the Updated NIH Criteria for Evaluating Research Grant Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Q&A addressing common questions about the updated review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical clarification on applying the updated criteria; useful for both reviewers and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict Of Interest, Confidentiality And Non Disclosure Rules For NIH Peer Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing conflicts of interest, confidentiality, and non-disclosure for NIH peer reviewers of grant applications and R&D contract proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance and forms (PDF/MS Word) for reviewers to certify compliance; critical for maintaining integrity of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Pre-Review Certification Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Form requiring reviewers to certify relevant disclosures or compliance before participating in review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to document conflicts/confidentiality obligations prior to reviewing; reviewers must complete as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Post-Review Certification Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Form for reviewers to certify appropriate conduct after completing reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides documentation that reviewer obligations were met post-meeting; may be used in oversight and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Instructions to Reviewers for Evaluating Research Involving Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions specific to reviewers on how to evaluate human-subjects protections in grant and cooperative agreement applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess protections, consent, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and monitoring plans per these instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important Notice to Applicants: Requirements for Human and Animal Subjects Research
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH notices specifying requirements for human and animal subjects research to be met in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet these requirements; reviewers should confirm compliance or note concerns during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Decision Trees for Human Subject Protection and Inclusion Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-tree tools to assist reviewers in handling human-subject protection and inclusion questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured steps for determining review actions related to inclusion/protection; useful during SRG deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Humans
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials addressing human-subject protection policies and considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include PDFs and PowerPoint resources outlining expectations for protecting human participants in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women in Clinical Research / Women in NIH-Defined Phase III Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance documents addressing inclusion and analysis of women in clinical research and Phase III trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reviewers to evaluate appropriate inclusion, subgroup analyses, and reporting plans for women participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minorities in Clinical Research / Minorities in NIH-Defined Phase III Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on inclusion and evaluation of minority participants in clinical research and Phase III trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should verify inclusion plans and appropriate analysis for minority groups per NIH policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children in Human Subjects Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on inclusion/consideration of children as research participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess justification, protections, and compliance with NIH policies related to pediatric research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on required data and safety monitoring plans for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate adequacy of monitoring plans, DSMBs where appropriate, and safety oversight mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Regulations (42 CFR Part 52h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal regulations governing the scientific peer review of research grant applications and research (Final Rules and Federal Register notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/regulatory baseline that frames peer review practices; reviewers and administrators must comply with these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Notes (CSR publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR publication containing developments related to NIH review policies and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks policy updates and practical notes for reviewers and SRG administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical guidance on Rating of Grant Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical documents and reports about rating of grant applications, including explicit statements of review criteria (e.g., June 1997 announcements, PROG deliberations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides context for evolution of current criteria; useful for understanding prior expectations and regulatory responses.
